summary:
Galaxy Explorer is an inclusive space education platform designed for people of all ages, from 3 to 100. Our project aims to make complex NASA space and Earth data easier to understand, explore, and enjoy. It addresses accessibility barriers in traditional science education, especially for young children, older adults, and people with visual or hearing impairments.

For children aged 3–5, the platform offers playful mini-games, shape-matching activities, and cheerful audio cues. For older learners, it provides interactive 3D orbital models and NASA Earthdata. It also includes special accessibility modes: high-contrast captions for hearing-impaired users and voice narration with screen-reader guidance for visually impaired users.

Galaxy Explorer is important because space education should be accessible to everyone, regardless of age or ability. Our goal is to make space discovery more inclusive, engaging, and available worldwide.
details:
Galaxy Explorer is an inclusive space education platform designed to make space science accessible to everyone, from ages 3 to 100. It transforms complex NASA space and Earth data into interactive, understandable, and enjoyable learning experiences.

The platform works through age-adaptive learning features. Children aged 3–5 can explore space using playful mini-games, shape-matching activities, and audio cues. Older learners can discover interactive 3D orbital models and NASA Earthdata. It also provides two accessibility modes: high-contrast captions and descriptive subtitles for hearing-impaired users, and voice narration with screen-reader guidance for visually impaired users.

The main benefits are equal access to science education, improved space literacy, and more engaging learning experiences. Our intended impact is to reduce accessibility barriers and make space discovery available worldwide.

Our project creatively combines adaptive education, interactive space exploration, open NASA data, and accessibility features in one platform. Our team considered different age groups, sensory disabilities, user privacy, ease of use, and global accessibility. We designed the project with zero collection of personal data from users under 18 and avoided using NASA logos. AI-generated interface graphics are visibly identified with watermarks.

Our future development plan includes school pilot programs, multilingual voice narration, improved captions, and open-source educational modules for worldwide use.
